summary: Return the fixed J=8 or J=12 complex residue and pole tables with conjugate completion.

capability: Return the fixed J=8 or J=12 complex residue and pole tables with conjugate completion.
operation: integer pole count J to residues and complex pole positions
discovery.model: rational approximation of the Maxwellian plasma dispersion function
discovery.boundary: only the frozen J=8 and J=12 tables exist; no interpolation or extrapolation

identity.relation: integer pole count J to residues and complex pole positions
identity.direction: integer pole count J to residues and complex pole positions
identity.definition: Z(zeta) is approximated by sum_j bzj[j]/(zeta-czj[j]); the stored first half is completed by conjugation and negative conjugation, respectively.
identity.model: rational approximation of the Maxwellian plasma dispersion function
identity.coordinates: dimensionless complex zeta plane; one pole axis
identity.boundary: only the frozen J=8 and J=12 tables exist; no interpolation or extrapolation
assumptions: Input units and normalization follow the declared ports; no physical parameters are inferred.

inputs.name: j_order
inputs.description: Pole order J, selecting one fixed residue/position table and fixing the returned array length and the pole-block size of each species
inputs.constraints: Only 8 or 12 is allowed, corresponding to the source's 8-pole and 12-pole tables; other orders have no table in the source and must fail closed.

outputs.name: bzj
outputs.description: Pole residues used by the matrix to weight the resonance term along the pole axis
outputs.constraints: Finite complex; the second half must equal the conjugate of the first half.

outputs.name: czj
outputs.description: Pole positions giving the complex resonance offsets and entering the denominator of the resonance argument
outputs.constraints: Finite complex; the second half must equal the negative conjugate of the first half.

outputs.name: j_order
outputs.description: Pole order actually used in this call, echoing the input so the caller can check the matrix blocking

outputs.name: half_order
outputs.description: Number of first-half poles `J/2` fixed by the source, used to check the conjugate-completion boundary

outputs.name: sum_bzj
outputs.description: Sum of residues, used to check the zeroth-moment condition

outputs.name: sum_bzcj
outputs.description: Sum of residue-pole-position products, used to check the first-moment condition

outputs.name: sum_bzcj2
outputs.description: Sum of residue-pole-position-squared products, used to check the second-moment condition

preconditions: only the frozen J=8 and J=12 tables exist; no interpolation or extrapolation
supported: Return the fixed J=8 or J=12 complex residue and pole tables with conjugate completion.
excluded: No mode identity or arbitrary-parameter accuracy is inferred beyond the declared numerical method.

failure_semantics.invalid_input: Raises ValueError for declared invalid inputs; numeric conversion errors may propagate for unsupported Python objects.
failure_semantics.runtime_failure: Numerical backend errors propagate; no fallback relation is substituted.
failure_semantics.nonconvergence: Not applicable; no iterative root solve is exposed.
failure_semantics.partial_results: No partial mapping is returned after an exception.

example.code:
from scirel.kinetic import get_z_pole_coefficients
r=get_z_pole_coefficients(j_order=8); assert len(r['bzj'])==8 and len(r['czj'])==8
example.expected: The asserted result follows the declared output contract.
